When Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit he stayed silent until revelation came saying its knowledge is with his Lord and people are given little knowledge.
Ibn Abbas said the verse on neither loud nor low prayer meant reciting so the pagans of Mecca would not hear and abuse the Quran; Aisha said it concerned invocations.
When the Prophet asked Ali and Fatima why they did not pray at night, Ali said they rise when Allah wills, and the Prophet recited that man is most quarrelsome.
Moses, rebuked for claiming to be most learned, sought Al-Khadir at the junction of the two seas but could not stay patient over the boat, the boy and the wall.
Moses, rebuked for calling himself the most learned, travels with his attendant to meet Al-Khadir, who scuttles a boat, kills a boy and repairs a wall before they part.
The greatest losers of verse 18.103 are said to be the Jews, who disbelieved Muhammad, and the Christians, who denied Paradise's food and drink, not Al-Haruriyya, the pledge-breakers.
On the Day of Resurrection a huge fat man weighs nothing with Allah, and Death is brought as a ram and slaughtered, leaving Paradise's and Hell's people eternity without death.
The Prophet asks Gabriel why he does not visit more often, and the verse is revealed that the angels descend only by their Lord's command.
Al-As bin Wail will not pay Khabbab's debt unless he disbelieves in Muhammad, saying if resurrected he will have wealth and children to pay with; verses about him are revealed.
Moses blames Adam for people's expulsion from Paradise and Adam wins, it being written before his creation; Muslims are told to fast Ashura, the day Moses defeated Pharaoh.
Abdullah says Bani Israel, Al-Kahf, Maryam, Taha and Al-Anbiya are among the very old surahs he learnt by heart, his first property.
People are gathered barefoot and naked, Abraham clothed first, some of the Prophet's companions are taken away, and Adam must send 999 of every thousand to the Fire.
Verse 22.11 describes a man who came to Medina and called Islam good when his wife bore a son and his mares foaled, and bad when they did not.
The verse on two opponents disputing about their Lord was revealed about those who went out to fight at Badr, Ali, Hamza and Ubaida against Utba, Shaiba and Al-Walid.
Husbands who accuse their wives of adultery, told to bring witnesses or be lashed, carry out the revealed mutual cursing; the couples separate and the child goes to the mother.
Aisha tells of the forged story spread about her by Abdullah bin Ubai, her grief until Allah revealed her innocence, Abu Bakr resuming aid to Mistah, and Hassan's visits.
When the verse telling women to draw their veils over their bosoms came, the early emigrant women cut their garments and covered their heads and faces with them.
Asked whether disbelievers will be gathered on their faces, the Prophet says the One who made them walk on their feet can make them walk on their faces.
The greatest sins are setting up a rival to Allah, killing one's son lest he share one's food, and adultery with a neighbour's wife, as a verse then confirmed.
Ibn Abbas holds that verse 4.93 on deliberately killing a believer was never cancelled and allows no repentance, while verses 25.68-70, with their repentance, concerned the pagans.
Abdullah names five things already past: the Smoke, the Moon, the Romans, the Mighty Grasp and the constant punishment.
On the Day of Resurrection Abraham sees his father's darkened face and reminds Allah of His promise not to disgrace him, and Allah says He has forbidden Paradise to disbelievers.
Told to warn his near kindred, the Prophet calls Quraysh from Safa and warns each clan and relative that he cannot save them from Allah; Abu Lahab curses him.
On his deathbed Abu Talib refuses to declare none worthy of worship but Allah, and verses forbid seeking forgiveness for pagans and say Allah alone guides whom He will.
Ibn Abbas explains that 'will bring you home' in verse 28.85 means to Mecca.
Ibn Mas'ud rebukes a speaker's claim about the Smoke, explaining it as what starving Quraysh saw in famine, with the Mighty Grasp at Badr and the Romans' defeat already past.
Every child is born on the Fitra and his parents make him Jewish, Christian or Magian; the Prophet then recites the verse on the nature Allah created mankind with.
Troubled that none is free of wrong, the companions are told the wrong in verse 6.82 means joining others in worship with Allah, as Luqman told his son.
A man asks the Prophet what faith, Islam and Ihsan are and when the Hour comes, hears its portents, and the Prophet says it was Gabriel teaching people their religion.
The Prophet says the keys of the Unseen are five and recites that the knowledge of the Hour is with Allah alone.
Allah has prepared for His pious servants what no eye has seen, no ear heard and no one imagined, as the verse on joy kept hidden for them says.
The Prophet is closest to every believer; a dead believer's property goes to his heirs, but his debts and poor children are to be brought to the Prophet.
Zaid bin Haritha was called Zaid bin Muhammad until the verse came telling believers to call adopted sons by their fathers' names.
Anas thinks the verse on believers true to their covenant with Allah was revealed about Anas bin An-Nadr.
While collecting the Quran into copies, Zaid bin Thabit found a missing verse of Surat al-Ahzab only with Khuzaima, whose witness the Prophet counted as two men's.
Told to give his wives a choice, the Prophet starts with Aisha, who chooses Allah and His Messenger; verses also concern Zainab and Zaid and setting aside a wife's turn.
Umar urges veiling the Prophet's wives; guests lingering after the Prophet's wedding feast for Zainab lead to the verse of the screen, and women are allowed out for their needs.
After the veil was ordered, Aisha is told to admit Aflah, her uncle through the wife of Abi Al-Qu'ais who nursed her, as foster relations count like blood.
Asked how to invoke Allah for him, the Prophet teaches the words asking Allah to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham's family.
The Prophet links Moses' shyness to the verse telling believers not to be like those who annoyed Moses, whom Allah cleared of what they alleged.
